artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Section 13 records the write-absence together with what would have shown one.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: ZERO writes, uploads or site mutations occurred, evidenced (the absence asserted with what would have shown one).
acceptance.invocation: Full session tool-call record reviewed for upload_text_to_site / save_email_attachment_to_site; list_site_files re-run against the Shared site after all reads and compared on lastModifiedDateTime and etag.
acceptance.output_evidence: upload_text_to_site: 0 invocations. save_email_attachment_to_site: 0 invocations. NEITHER WRITE TOOL WAS EVEN LOADED into the session tool set. Calls actually made against this surface, all read-class: 1 whoami, 2 find_sharepoint_site, 3 list_site_drives, 4 list_site_files, 1 read_site_workbook, 1 read_site_file, 1 profile_site_file, 1 read_document. WHAT WOULD HAVE SHOWN A WRITE: every call in this session appears in the record with its returned payload -- the reads are all visible, including ones that returned a structured refusal rather than content -- so a write call would have been equally visible. Independently, re-listing the Shared site after the reads returns unchanged lastModifiedDateTime and etag on every entry, so nothing under this identity moved. The absence is MEASURED, not merely unobserved.
acceptance.denominator: 0 write-class calls of the 2 write-class tools that exist on this surface; 14 read-class calls made.

mutant.description: Observation-channel positive control: an assertion of zero writes is worthless if a write would not have been visible in the first place. Confirmed the channel records calls of the same family by checking that the READ calls -- same tool family, same session, same transport -- are all present with their payloads.
mutant.expected: If the record captures read calls and their payloads, it would have captured a write call and its payload.
mutant.observed: All 14 read-class calls are present with returned payloads, including the PDF binary-hint response, which proves the channel records non-content responses too and not only successes. A write would therefore not have been silently absent.

determinism.method: Shared site listing re-read after all read operations and compared against the pre-read listing.
determinism.observed: Identical lastModifiedDateTime and etag values across entries; no item mutated.

declared_exclusions.reason: READ-ONLY wave. Andrew's readonly instruction scopes the whole access-layer program and the TO puts both write tools OUT OF SCOPE. Testing a write to prove it works would itself be the violation.

declared_exclusions.item: Any proposal to widen the bg-concierge-gate G4 identity fence
declared_exclusions.reason: The TO fences it explicitly: report what the reach IS; an entitlement change is Andrew's, not a W7 deliverable. If the honest conclusion is that the concierge cannot reach a class, that is a FINDING and a good one.

surprises: The gateway identity is Andrew Berman personally rather than a service principal, so every call on this surface attributes to him -- worth knowing before anything here is scheduled or made production-facing.

compiler_tools.result: Write-absence evidenced AGAINST THE OBSERVATION CHANNEL rather than asserted -- the channel was first shown to record same-family calls.
